item.title: 🔵 Ghostwriter Targets Ukrainian Government With Geofenced PDF Phishing, Cobalt Strike
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and user awareness training.
The Belarus-aligned threat group known as Ghostwriter has been attributed to a fresh set of attacks targeting governmental organizations in Ukraine. Active since at least 2016, Ghostwriter has been linked to both cyber espionage and influence operations targeting neighboring countries, particularly Ukraine. It's also tracked under the monikers FrostyNeighbor, PUSHCHA, Storm-0257, TA445, UAC‑0057

Source: The Hacker News  |  Severity: FYI  |  Age: 1d ago

item.title: 🟠 Windows Zero-Days Expose BitLocker Bypasses And CTFMON Privilege Escalation
item.description:
Why this matters: Privilege escalation risk — review local admin exposure and endpoint controls.
An anonymous cybersecurity researcher who disclosed three Microsoft Defender vulnerabilities has returned with two more zero-days involving a BitLocker bypass and a privilege escalation impacting Windows Collaborative Translation Framework (CTFMON). The security defects have been codenamed YellowKey and GreenPlasma, respectively, by the researcher, who goes by the online aliases Chaotic Eclipse

item.title: 🔵 Simple bypass of the link preview function in Outlook Junk folder, (Thu, May 14th)
item.description:
Why this matters: Could impact email access or mail flow — monitor delivery and client issues.

Besides serving as a place where Microsoft Outlook places suspected spam, the Outlook Junk folder has one additional function that can be quite helpful when it comes to identifying malicious messages. Any e-mail placed in this folder is stripped of all formatting, and destinations of all links included in the message become visible to the user, as you can see in the following images which show the same e-mail when it is placed in the inbox, and when it is placed in the Junk folder.



Source: SANS Internet Storm Center  |  Severity: FYI  |  Age: 1d ago
